classifiedFindings.label: M-01
classifiedFindings.title: migrate() unbounded per-unit mint loop causes gas DoS for large V1 holders

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. V1 NFTs retain their original utility (migrate() is the only affected flow and it burns then re-mints atomically). Impact is unavailability of the migration path for any holder whose aggregate V1 ERC1155 balance at a single index is large enough that 'balance' iterations of v2.mintFor exceed the block gas limit.
attackPath: 1. A user legitimately accumulates a large balance of a single V1 index (NFTMigrator.sol:66 reads IERC1155.balanceOf(msg.sender, i)).
3. The inner loop 'for (j = 0; j < balance; j++) v2.mintFor(v2Index, msg.sender)' (lines 70-72) performs one external _mint per unit held.
4. There is no batch mintFor and no pagination; migrate() processes the caller's ENTIRE balance in a single transaction.
5. For a sufficiently large balance, the cumulative gas exceeds the block gas limit and migrate() always reverts, leaving the holder permanently unable to migrate.
classification.likelihood: medium - requires a holder to have accumulated a large single-index balance; no special privilege needed (permissionless availability issue, balance is not owner-controlled).
classification.assumptions: A V1 holder's single-index balance is large enough that 'balance' sequential ERC1155 _mint operations exceed the block gas limit.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond ordinary block gas limits.

classifiedFindings.justification: Protocol function (migration) becomes unavailable for affected holders with no in-contract workaround (no paginated/partial migrate path). Assets are not directly at risk because V1 NFTs are unaffected and remain usable, so this caps at Medium per C4 (function/availability impacted, no asset theft). Not High: there is no asset loss or theft, V1 utility is retained, and 'permanently stuck funds' would require demonstrating that V1 NFTs lose all value when un-migratable, which is not shown in scope.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE for severity-auditor: depends on whether realistic single-index balances can plausibly reach the gas ceiling. If the realistic max balance per index is small (e.g. capped supply per dispatcher), this collapses toward Low/QA (merely expensive, not a brick). Conversely, if some V1 indexes have large per-holder balances, Medium is firm. Auditor should confirm realistic balance distribution and per-_mint gas cost.

classifiedFindings.label: M-02
classifiedFindings.title: Late V1 dispatcher registration bricks migrate() for affected holders via index-0 mintFor revert

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Migration becomes unavailable for holders of any V1 index registered after the migrator was initialized. V1 NFTs retain their utility. State is recoverable by a migrator-owner action.
attackPath: 1. Migrator owner configures mappings for all current V1 indexes and calls setInitialized() (NFTMigrator.sol:51-58), which validates indexMapping only for indexes 1..v1.nextIndex()-1 AT THAT TIME and is one-way.
2. Later, the V1 NFTMinter owner (a distinct trust principal from the migrator owner) registers a new dispatcher, incrementing v1.nextIndex() (NFTMinter.sol:127-128).
3. The migrator's indexMapping[newIndex] is still 0 (never set; setInitialized cannot be re-run meaningfully and did not cover newIndex).
4. A holder of newIndex calls migrate(); the loop reaches i=newIndex, burns the V1 NFTs (NFTMigrator.sol:68), then calls v2.mintFor(0, msg.sender) because indexMapping[newIndex]==0 (line 69-71).
5. mintFor reverts at 'NFTMinterV2: index not registered' (NFTMinterV2.sol:208) since configs[0].dispatcher==address(0) (V2 nextIndex starts at 1).

6. The entire migrate() tx reverts (the burn is rolled back), so the holder of newIndex cannot migrate until the mapping is fixed. Holders of other indexes are unaffected (balance==0 at newIndex skips the iteration).
classification.likelihood: medium - requires post-initialization V1 dispatcher registration by the V1 owner; cross-contract ordering coupling, not a single-owner reckless mistake.
classification.assumptions: V1 owner registers a new dispatcher after the migrator is initialized, and at least one user holds that new index.
classification.externalRequirements: Action by the independently-owned V1 NFTMinter contract owner after migrator initialization.

classifiedFindings.justification: Availability of the migration flow is impacted for a subset of holders due to cross-contract ordering coupling between two independently-owned contracts (not pure single-owner self-harm, so KI-1/KI-4 do not fully absorb it). No assets are stolen or permanently lost: V1 NFTs remain usable and the migrator owner can restore migration by calling setMapping(newIndex, validV2Index). The recoverability and partial scope keep this firmly at Medium (function/availability impact), not High.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE for severity-auditor: this is recoverable by the migrator owner adding the missing mapping, and the trigger is a privileged V1-owner action. If the auditor treats the cross-contract coupling as fully covered by owner-trust (V1 owner expected to coordinate with migrator owner), this could drop to Low/QA. Kept at Medium because the two owners are distinct trust principals and migrate() silently bricks (burns-then-reverts) rather than degrading gracefully.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: NFTMinterV2._executeMint lacks ReentrancyGuard (cross-index re-entry not blocked)

classification.assetImpact: None today. No in-scope path is exploitable: in-scope hooks make no external calls in onDispatch, and BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch only forceApprove + ERC4626.deposit. A re-entrant mint would be a fully-paid mint.
attackPath: Latent: dispatch() nonReentrant guard lives on the dispatcher (ATokenDispatcherV2.sol:118-126), so re-entry into _executeMint targeting a DIFFERENT dispatcher index is not blocked by a guard on NFTMinterV2 itself (170-201). No current in-scope dispatcher makes a re-entrant external call, so it is not exploitable today.
classification.assumptions: Would require a future/added dispatcher whose onDispatch makes a re-entrant external call.
classification.externalRequirements: A re-entrancy-capable dispatcher that does not currently exist in scope.

classifiedFindings.justification: Missing guard is a real, present property of in-scope code (concrete root cause and concrete fix), but no current in-scope path makes it exploitable. Defense-in-depth hardening -> Low.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: setRatio accepts ratio == MAX_RATIO, contradicting documented strict-less-than invariant

classification.assetImpact: None. Spec/code deviation only; truncation in added=amount*ratio/100 rounds in the harmless direction.
attackPath: setRatio uses 'if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert' (BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.sol:93) while NatSpec/invariant states strictly < MAX_RATIO=50 (lines 29,47,91); ratio==50 is wrongly accepted.

classifiedFindings.justification: Genuine spec-vs-code deviation of a stated invariant with no asset impact -> Low (state/spec correctness). Owner-set parameter, but the issue is correctness of the documented bound, not owner abuse.

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: Donation swap uses limitRaw=0 relying solely on a pooler-supplied minUSDC floor (no on-chain oracle/TWAP reference)

classification.assetImpact: Bounded to the donation slice destined for the owner-configured batchMinter flow, not user deposits. pool() is onlyAuthorizedPooler + whenNotPaused + nonReentrant; minUSDC is supplied by that same semi-trusted pooler at call time.
attackPath: BalancerPoolerV2.sol:214-243 swaps with limitRaw=0 and only the pooler-provided minUSDC as slippage protection; no independent on-chain price reference. A pooler passing minUSDC=0 is itself a role mistake.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a semi-trusted pooler to supply a weak/zero floor.
classification.assumptions: Authorized pooler is semi-trusted per project trust model.
classification.externalRequirements: Authorized-pooler action with a weak minUSDC; value at risk is the owner-configured donation flow.

classifiedFindings.justification: Downgraded from Medium by sanitizer: protection is delegated to an off-chain-chosen floor supplied by a semi-trusted role, and the value at risk is an owner/role-governed donation slice rather than user funds. Residual concern (no on-chain TWAP reference) is real hardening -> Low.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-01
classifiedFindings.title: Missing zero-address validation in constructors (NFTMigrator, BurnerV2, GatherV2)

classification.assetImpact: None. Deployment misconfiguration only (downstream calls revert if a critical address is zero).
attackPath: Constructors accept critical addresses without zero-address checks; a zero address bricks the flow at use time.

classifiedFindings.justification: Code-hardening recommendation, no attack path -> QA bundle.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-02
classifiedFindings.title: Unchecked ERC4626 deposit return value in BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch

classification.assetImpact: None. pool() re-reads balanceOf(address(this)) (BalancerPoolerV2.sol:192) rather than the deposit return, so accounting uses actual held sUSDS.
attackPath: IERC4626(sUSDS).deposit return is ignored at line 183; bounded because subsequent logic does not rely on it.

classifiedFindings.justification: Accounting-hygiene hardening with bounded/no impact -> QA.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-03
classifiedFindings.title: abi.encodePacked used to build dynamic-string metadata in uri() (cosmetic)

classification.assetImpact: None. The packed output (NFTMinterV2.sol:262-273) is returned as a metadata JSON string and is never hashed; no collision/identity impact materializes.
attackPath: No security path; original collision concern was based on a misread (no keccak256 on this output).

classifiedFindings.justification: Cosmetic style note (prefer abi.encode for dynamic-string concatenation clarity), no security impact -> QA.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-04
classifiedFindings.title: setMinter emits no event (and V2 uses single-step Ownable)

attackPath: setMinter (ATokenDispatcherV2.sol:85) changes a privileged role without emitting an event, hindering off-chain detection; V2 Ownable is single-step (Ownable2Step would guard a transfer mistake, but reckless-admin mistakes are known-invalid).

classifiedFindings.justification: Missing-event half is a legitimate monitorability QA point independent of owner trust; Ownable2Step half is reckless-admin-adjacent (known-invalid) and folded in as a minor note -> QA.

classifiedFindings.label: C-01
classifiedFindings.title: Owner can replaceDispatcher at an existing index, re-pointing token/metadata under existing holders

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrable in scope. replaceDispatcher (NFTMinterV2.sol:227-247) is onlyOwner and changes the dispatcher/token/metadata for an index with existing holders; any 'redemption honored against new token' impact lives in an external redemption layer (OOS).
attackPath: Owner calls replaceDispatcher(index, newDispatcher); existing holders' tokenId now maps to a different dispatcher/token. No in-scope on-chain redemption keys off the mapping, so no in-scope value impact is demonstrable.
classification.externalRequirements: None in scope; impact would require an external redemption layer.

classifiedFindings.justification: Pure centralization/design-soundness note: wholly owner-gated, no in-scope value impact -> Centralization (C-01) in the QA bundle.

excluded.reason: Hard-suppressed by sanitizer (KI-1/KI-4 owner-driven + C4-STD speculation on out-of-scope external phUSD backing; no permissionless extraction path). Not classified.
